observations.code_quote: **Custom property columns** surface the team's `CustomPropertyDefinition`s (loaded in `accountsColumnConfigLogic` via the generated `customPropertyDefinitionsList`) as a "Custom properties" picker group. Each is selected as ``accounts.custom_properties.values.`<definition-id>` AS cp_<id>`` — a JSON dot-access through the `custom_properties` lazy join on `system.accounts` (backed by the `customer_analytics_custompropertyvalue` EAV table; one JOIN regardless of column count). Because the alias is an opaque `cp_<id>`, every label-bearing surface must resolve it back via the `aliasToDefinition` selector: the table header (`useContextColumns` in `AccountsHogQLTable`) and the configurator's "Visible columns" list (`SelectedAccountColumn`). Cells render by display type (`CustomPropertyCell`: date→`TZLabel`, boolean→icon, select→`LemonColorGlyph` + label, numeric→`formatCustomPropertyValue`). Sorting a numeric custom property (display type `number`/`currency`/`percent`) casts the (string) JSON value with `toFloatOrNull(...)` in the `orderBy` — see `orderByExpression` in `accountsLogic`, driven by `aliasToDefinition` — so numbers sort by magnitude rather than lexically; non-numeric types sort by the alias directly. The stored sort state (URL hash, saved views) keeps the clean column name; the cast is applied only at query-build time. Numeric custom properties are also selectable in the **overview tiles** sum/avg/min/max/median/threshold pickers — `numericColumnOptions` recognizes the display type and wraps the value in `toFloatOrNull(...)` the same way so aggregation is numeric.

observations.code_quote: - `DefaultTooltip` (the built-in tooltip, also usable from a custom `tooltip` render prop) takes optional `valueFormatter`, `labelFormatter`, `labelRenderer`, `showHeader`, `showTotal`, `totalLabel`, `totalFormatter`, `sortedByValue`, `hideZeroRows`, `onRowClick`, and `footer`. `valueFormatter` gets `(value, entry)` — the row's `seriesData` entry as a second arg — so each row can format with its own `series.meta` (e.g. per-column currency/duration); it may return a node, not just a string (e.g. a property-formatted value). `labelFormatter` transforms the raw x-axis label shown in the tooltip header (e.g. convert an ISO datetime string to "Jun 24, 10:00"); on time-series charts with `xAxis.timezone` + `interval` set it defaults to an interval-aware date formatter that includes the weekday for single-day buckets ("Sat, Jun 6, 2026", "Sat, Jun 6, 14:00"; week/month buckets span days, so "Jun 1, 2026", "Jun 2026"), so the header matches the auto-formatted axis ticks — an explicit `labelFormatter` still wins. `labelRenderer` overrides how each row's label renders (defaults to the series label) — use for richer labels than a plain string, e.g. breakdown-value pills. `showHeader` (default true) toggles the header label row — pass false for charts without a meaningful header (pie slices, aggregated single-column bars). `showTotal` appends a footer row summing the visible series; it excludes `overlay` series (goal lines) and series with `visibility.total: false` (values that don't sum meaningfully with the rest, e.g. a percentage column alongside counts — the row itself still renders) from the sum, and is suppressed when fewer than two summable series remain. `totalFormatter` formats the total (defaults to `valueFormatter` applied with the first summable row's entry); `totalLabel` defaults to `'Total'`. `sortedByValue` sorts rows by value descending so the highest value appears first. `hideZeroRows` drops rows whose value is exactly `0` (e.g. lifecycle statuses absent for a period), so the tooltip lists only series with data at the hovered point. `onRowClick` makes each series row clickable (firing with the row's `seriesData` entry) — the tooltip must be pinned for clicks to land, since an unpinned tooltip is `pointer-events: none`; use it to open a per-series drill-down (e.g. the persons modal). `footer` renders arbitrary content below all rows (with a divider) — useful for "click to inspect" hints. A formatter taking only `value` stays compatible — the extra arg is ignored. Pinned tooltips are copy-friendly: outside-dismissal keys off where the press _started_ (pointer-down outside the tooltip/chart, or Escape), so a text-selection drag that releases outside the tooltip doesn't dismiss it, and a click that completes a text selection inside a row doesn't fire `onRowClick`.

observations.code_quote: - **Examples are one row per report at its birth, by default.** For partition `dt=D` the examples asset reads the report-state and labels snapshots `dt=D-lookback..D` and emits one row per report, on the snapshot of the day it was created, labeled from the snapshot `horizon_days` later (3 for open, 7 for action / pr_created / discuss, 14 for dismiss_wrong / pr_merged / refund). Features are built by the feature set from that snapshot's state columns plus `age_hours`, the report's age at the snapshot. Labels are aligned to the state spine, so a report with no label event is a negative (all-zero labels), not absent. Label-only rows (no Postgres state) are skipped, as are state rows read long after their snapshot day (backfills carry current Postgres state; see `features_observed_at`) and, for the `dismiss_wrong` head, rows whose status telemetry fails the dataset's `label_provenance_ok` check. Birth is the moment serving scores a report, and the label that comes out is a per-report probability, which is what the inbox ordering needs. A report born before the window, or one whose birth-day snapshot is missing from it, is no example; `reports_missing_birth_snapshot` on the asset counts the second case, which is a gap in the partitions.
